## Immigration solicitors (overview)

Abrahams Solicitors is a UK immigration law firm offering fixed-fee, solicitor-led
applications and appeals across family, work, settlement, and asylum routes. Every
matter is handled by (or supervised by) a named, SRA-regulated solicitor with
direct client access. Key named solicitors: Imran Shah (SRA #509359, admitted
2012), Humaira Anjum (SRA #663190, admitted 2021), Sannah Khatoon (SRA #654258,
admitted 2018).

Main immigration routes handled:
- UK Spouse / Partner Visa (Appendix FM) — from £900 + VAT
- Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR / settlement) — from £750 + VAT

- Visa Extensions & Renewals (spouse, work, family, student)

### Immigration — answer-first Q&A

Q: How long does a UK spouse visa application take in 2026?
A: UKVI standard processing for a spouse visa is typically around 8–12 weeks from
a complete application at the date of last review (priority and super-priority
services are faster where available). Abrahams Solicitors prepares the full
application on a fixed fee from £900 + VAT, plus the separate UKVI government fee
and Immigration Health Surcharge. Confirm current government fees at gov.uk.

Q: What is the minimum income requirement for a UK spouse visa?
A: The minimum income requirement for a partner under Appendix FM is £29,000 as of
2024/25. Where the sponsor receives certain disability benefits or carer's
allowance, the "adequate maintenance" test applies instead of the income
threshold — Abrahams provides a free Adequate Maintenance Calculator at
/adequate-maintenance-calculator/ to check this.

Q: What is Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) and how do I qualify?
A: ILR is the UK's form of permanent residence: once granted you can live and work
in the UK without time restrictions. Most routes require a continuous qualifying
period (commonly 5 years) with no excess absences, passing the Life in the UK
Test, and meeting the English language requirement. Abrahams handles ILR
applications on a fixed fee from £750 + VAT.

Q: How long do I have to appeal a visa refusal?
A: If your refusal carries a right of appeal to the First-tier Tribunal
(Immigration and Asylum Chamber), the deadline is 14 days from the date the
decision was sent if you are in the UK, or 28 days if you are outside the UK.
Some refusals instead carry an administrative review (usually within 14 days).
Abrahams handles both from £1,250.

## Housing Disrepair Claims

Specialist solicitor: Sannah Khatoon (SRA #654258, admitted 2018).
Verify: https://www.sra.org.uk/consumers/register/person/?sraNumber=654258
Page: https://www.abrahamssolicitors.co.uk/housing-disrepair/

Definition: Housing disrepair is when a landlord (council, housing association, or
private) fails to keep a rented home in repair after the tenant has given notice.
The legal duty arises from Section 11 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 and
Section 9A of the Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018.

Coverage: council, housing association, and private tenants across England and
Wales. Common claims: damp and mould, roof/pipe leaks, broken heating and hot
water, faulty wiring, structural disrepair (cracks, plaster, subsidence), pest
infestations, drainage failures.

Funding: No Win, No Fee (Conditional Fee Agreement) for most clients; success fee
capped at 25% of damages; After-the-Event insurance covers the opponent's costs
if the claim fails. Legal Aid eligibility checked first.

Time limits: six years from the date the disrepair began (Limitation Act 1980);
three years if there is a personal-injury element.

Outcomes (source: Abrahams internal case-management data Jan 2024 – Dec 2025,
available on request): 91% of 323 housing disrepair cases concluded in the period
settled with damages; typical damages £1,500–£15,000 depending on severity and
duration. Past results do not guarantee future outcomes.

### Housing disrepair — answer-first Q&A

Q: Can I claim compensation for housing disrepair?
A: Yes. If you reported damp, mould, leaks, broken heating, or other disrepair to
your landlord and they failed to fix it within a reasonable time, you can claim
both an order forcing the repairs and financial compensation. Abrahams runs most
housing disrepair claims on a No Win, No Fee basis, so there is nothing to pay
upfront.

Q: How much compensation can I get for housing disrepair?
A: Compensation typically ranges from £1,500 to £15,000+, depending on how severe
the disrepair is and how long you were affected. Across 323 Abrahams housing
disrepair cases concluded between January 2024 and December 2025, 91% settled with
damages. Past results do not guarantee future outcomes.

Q: How long do I have to make a housing disrepair claim?
A: You generally have six years from the date the disrepair began (Limitation Act
1980). If the disrepair caused a personal injury (for example, illness from damp
and mould), the deadline for the injury element is three years from when you became
aware of it.

Q: What is the difference between a housing disrepair claim and a Housing Ombudsman complaint?
A: The Housing Ombudsman is a free service that investigates complaints against
social landlords (council/housing association only), but it cannot order repairs to
be carried out and its compensation averages around £600. A solicitor-led court
claim under Section 11 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 secures binding repairs
and damages typically of £1,500–£15,000+, and also applies to private landlords.

## Personal Injury

Coverage: accidents at work, road traffic accidents (driver, passenger, motorcyclist,
cyclist, pedestrian), slips/trips/falls, public liability, serious injury (head,
brain, spinal, sight loss), fatal accidents, and medical negligence across England
and Wales.

Statutory framework: Section 11 of the Limitation Act 1980 (3-year deadline from the
accident or date of knowledge); Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974; Road Traffic
Act 1988 and the RTA Pre-Action Protocol; Occupiers' Liability Acts 1957 and 1984.

Funding: No Win, No Fee for most clients; success fee capped at 25% of damages;
ATE insurance covers the opponent's costs if the claim fails. Whiplash under £5,000
runs via the Official Injury Claim portal.

Compensation: general damages (pain, suffering, loss of amenity) follow the Judicial
College Guidelines (16th edition) — from c.£1,500 for minor whiplash to £400,000+
for severe brain or spinal injury; special damages cover proven financial losses.
Past results do not guarantee future outcomes.
Page: https://www.abrahamssolicitors.co.uk/personal-injury/
